title: Breathomics in depression: stress related changes of the exhaled breath during the early course of disease management
summary:
Background of the study
Depression is an illness that is usually associated with a loss of interest, anhedonia or low mood, and a lack of drive. In addition, there are other complaints such as problems in oncentration, feelings of insufficiency and worthlessness, suicidal thoughts, sleep disorders and suicidality. Currently, there are no objective measurement methods that would support the diagnosis of depression. 

It is now known that in depression there are also metabolic changes that are not only reflected in the brain but also in the body. Since the lungs are in close contact with the blood system and thus with the other organs, it is possible to measure metabolic products that are exhaled through the lungs and thus obtain information about the metabolism. 

The aim of the study is to determine whether the exhaled air of patients with depression contains molecules that can be clearly distinguished from non-diseased subjects and whether these change over time, e.g. also under the influence of dietary factors and medication. We would also like to investigate whether we could use these measurements to make statements about the severity of the impairment and whether certain therapy methods (e.g. certain drugs or certain psychotherapies) would be particularly helpful.  

Breath analysis is to be performed using a proton transfer reaction mass spectrometer (PTR-TOF-MS). The procedure is comparable to established breath tests (such as the alcohol or H2 breath test) and requires your active cooperation. Participants first breathe for 2 minutes at rest according to a predetermined rhythm. Then, after a deep breath, they first breath into a 1 liter bag (this air is discarded, as this is the air from the throat and bronchial tubes) and then immediately further the rest of the exhaled air into an air collection bag (so-called "Tedlar Bag"). Immediately after that, following the same procedure, they collect a 2nd breath into the air collection bag. The air can be stored in the air collection bag until it is analyzed. The collection of breath air takes place immediately after waking up and again 30 minutes and 60 minutes later. Around 8:30 a.m. we ask you to come to the clinic that day and bring the air collection bag and saliva samples (see below), which will be received by us and then analyzed by the PTR-TOF-MS method. 
At 9 o'clock in the morning in the clinic we ask some of the participants to deliver breath directly into the measuring device in the clinic and into 2 air collection bags in order to analyze if there are any differences between direct measurement and measurement from the air collected in the bag and to determine exactly the smallest substances that are in the breath with another measuring method. Furthermore, these test persons should also have an air sample collected from the environment in which the morning Tedlar bags were filled. They will be asked beforehand if these additional measurements are to be carried out.    
These measures do not involve any risks, they are not significantly time-consuming and they do not represent any particular burden.

In each case, immediately after collecting a breath sample, we ask the participants to provide a saliva sample, according to the instructions.  We would like to determine stress hormones in it and see if molecules from the breath are associated with stress hormones. On one occasion, we also ask female participants to provide a saliva sample to determine the hormones testosterone, estradiol and progesterone, which can be used to determine the phase of the menstrual cycle in women in order to investigate whether the hormones are associated with the molecules measured in the breath.  

In order to obtain comprehensive up-to-date information about complaints or state of health, participants will answer a standardized questionnaire in an interview with a study employee. The questionnaire collects general demographic data, such as age and gender, information on living conditions and lifestyle, as well as previous medical history. Participants will also be asked to complete a nutrition questionnaire, as diet can affect respiratory health. Furthermore, a physical examination with heart and lung examination as well as neurological status will be performed. In addition, a breath analysis (spirography) is performed. This involves determining airflow velocity and also lung volume on exhalation to assess lung function. Furthermore, mental status as well as strain and stress factors are assessed. Additionally, the pupillary light reflex will be recorded.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
MDD according to DSM-V, 
a MADRS depression severity score of larger than 26 
and age between 18 and 65 years.
Exclusion criteria:
Excluded will be patients with a current depressive episode with psychotic symptoms, and suicidal intend. 
Moreover, subjects with a known alcohol or drug dependency will be excluded. Neurological disorders and diseases affecting the brain function will further be excluded (e.g. manifest hypo- or hyperthyreodism). Patients with comorbid personality disorders and other axis 1 disorders will also be excluded.
